instruction: Determine whether bilevel optimization applies to the joint segmenter-decoder problem and identify practical ideas that can be tested without abandoning discrete RL.
scope: The segmenter is the upper-level policy; the projection and LoRA decoder are the inner learner that adapts to its boundary distribution.
sub_questions: What is the exact inner/outer formulation?
Can hard boundary sampling retain policy gradient in a bilevel loop?
Which approximation is practical for a LoRA-adapted LLM?
What failure modes make continuous boundary relaxations risky?

papers.title: Bilevel Programming for Hyperparameter Optimization and Meta-Learning
papers.authors: Luca Franceschi, Paolo Frasconi, Saverio Salzo, Riccardo Grazzi, Massimiliano Pontil
papers.problem: Differentiate an outer objective through an inner learning process.
papers.method: Makes approximate inner optimization dynamics part of the bilevel problem.
papers.results: Provides convergence conditions and empirical meta-learning evidence.
papers.relevance: Formal basis for treating the decoder as the inner learner.

papers.title: Truncated Back-propagation for Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Amirreza Shaban, Ching-An Cheng, Nathan Hatch, Byron Boots
papers.method: Backpropagates through only the latest few inner optimization steps.
papers.results: Few-step gradients often approached exact-gradient performance with lower memory and about half the compute in their experiments.
papers.relevance: Supports one-step decoder lookahead as a first diagnostic.

papers.title: Optimizing Millions of Hyperparameters by Implicit Differentiation
papers.authors: Jonathan Lorraine, Paul Vicol, David Duvenaud
papers.problem: Scale hypergradients to large parameter spaces.
papers.method: Combines the implicit function theorem with inverse-Hessian approximations.
papers.results: Reports only a few-times overhead over standard training for large hyperparameter networks.
papers.relevance: Possible later method, but risky for our non-convex decoder.

papers.title: DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
papers.authors: Hanxiao Liu, Karen Simonyan, Yiming Yang
papers.method: Uses a continuous relaxation and bilevel train/validation optimization.
papers.results: Reports competitive architectures at far lower search cost than prior discrete search.
papers.relevance: A soft-boundary template, but not deployment-equivalent to hard pooling.

papers.title: Understanding and Robustifying Differentiable Architecture Search
papers.authors: Arber Zela, Thomas Elsken, Tonmoy Saikia, Yassine Marrakchi, Thomas Brox, Frank Hutter
papers.problem: DARTS can collapse or generalize poorly.
papers.method: Relates failures to validation-loss curvature and tests regularization.
papers.results: Finds degenerate solutions across multiple search spaces and domains.
papers.relevance: Warns against assuming a soft segmentation proxy will discretize well.

papers.title: Learning to Reweight Examples for Robust Deep Learning
papers.authors: Mengye Ren, Wenyuan Zeng, Bin Yang, Raquel Urtasun
papers.problem: Learn training weights that improve clean validation performance.
papers.method: Uses validation loss after a one-step model update to meta-learn example weights.
papers.results: Improves robustness under class imbalance and label corruption.
papers.relevance: Precedent for support/query separation and one-step decoder adaptation.

papers.title: Probabilistic Bilevel Coreset Selection
papers.authors: Xiao Zhou, Renjie Pi, Weizhong Zhang, Yong Lin, Tong Zhang
papers.problem: Optimize a discrete subset based on performance of a model trained on it.
papers.method: Samples Bernoulli masks and applies an unbiased policy-gradient outer update after inner training.
papers.results: Reports gains over greedy subset selection, especially with noisy or imbalanced data.
papers.relevance: Closest algorithmic analogy for hard boundary selection with a post-adaptation reward.

papers.title: Bilevel Reinforcement Learning via the Development of Hyper-gradient without Lower-Level Convexity
papers.authors: Yan Yang, Bin Gao, Ya-xiang Yuan
papers.problem: Construct bilevel RL hypergradients without convex lower-level assumptions.
papers.method: Uses a regularized-RL fixed point to obtain fully first-order hypergradients.
papers.results: Provides model-based/model-free algorithms and convergence results.
papers.relevance: Confirms bilevel and RL can coexist, though its MDP structure differs from our decoder adaptation.

themes: Use a held-out outer objective after inner adaptation.
A few inner steps can be a useful approximation.
Policy gradient can optimize discrete outer selections without differentiating through the inner learner.
Continuous relaxations introduce a discretization and collapse risk.

gaps.statement: No current experiment measures boundary value after decoder adaptation.
gaps.evidence: The project training code scores sampled boundaries with the current detached decoder.

gaps.statement: Support/query separation has not been tested for segmenter rewards.
gaps.evidence: Current decoder CE and sampled-boundary rewards come from the same training stream.

gaps.statement: Hard-boundary policy-gradient bilevel training has not been studied in this acoustic-prefix setting.
gaps.evidence: Probabilistic coreset selection supplies a close method analogy, not a speech result.
